item.title: Should the Giants go all-in for the 2026 trade deadline’s biggest prize?
item.description: Jonathan Taylor | Getty Images Should the New York Giants go all-in at the NFL trade deadline to try and improve their chances of winning the NFC East this season? It’s a tricky question with defendable “yes” and “no” answers. Let’s look at both sides. Why they should go all-in The Giants are 4-2-1, leading a division where it looks like only one team — the Dallas Cowboys — is likely to really push them for the NFC East crown. The Giants, of course, already have a victory in hand. Despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart, star edge defender Brian Burns, and other key players the Giants have shown the resilience and toughness, what former Giants star and current radio analyst Carl Banks likes to call the “mental stamina” to make big plays in critical situations. “The players have earned the right,” GM Joe Schoen said on Tuesday, referring to the Giants having meaningful games coming up in November. “They were able to finish some of these games or make plays at the end of games or whatever it may be through their preparation and hard work and practice and dedication to the team and seeing how things play out on Sunday. So, they’ve earned that right to be in these games, and I know they’re excited about it.” They have also earned the right to have the organization support them by getting them some help, supplementing the roster in whatever way they can to give the team the best chance to finish what this gritty, under-manned, group has started. “We’re going to be in this thing until the end now,” head coach John Harbaugh said after Sunday’s overtime victory over the heavily-favored Houston Texans. Opportunities don’t come along every year, and sometimes they come along when you don’t expect them. The Philadelphia Eagles, NFC East champs three of the last four years, with a Super Bowl title and two Super Bowl appearances along the way, appear broken. GM Howie Roseman won’t let them stay that way. They will be back. Right now, though, their situation has opened a window in the division. The Washington Commanders don’t appear capable of taking advantage. The Cowboys probaby have more talent than the Giants, but do they have the grit, the resilience, and the coaching to get out of their own way long enough to be what they have the talent to be? The answer for most of the last 30 years or so has been “no.” The Giants aren’t paying Harbaugh $20 million annually to settle for seven wins when something bigger and more memorable is within reach, to say “no thanks, we’ll pass” when an opportunity to do something unexpectedly good comes along. They are paying Harbaugh to win. And, they are staring at a chance to do that, despite all of the obstacles that have been placed in their way. The Giants started down the “all-in” road by giving the Minnesota Vikings a 2027 fifth-round pick for J.J. McCarthy. The big “all-in” prize would be Indianapolis Colts’ running back Jonathan Taylor. item.title: Sal Stewart named 2026 Players Choice Awards NL Outstanding Rookie
item.description: TORONTO, ON - SEPTEMBER 25: Cincinnati Reds Infielder Sal Stewart (27) smiles during the MLB regular season game between the Cincinnati Reds and the Toronto Blue Jays on September 25, 2026, at Rogers Centre in Toronto, ON, Canada. (Photo by Julian Avram/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Major League Baseball Players Association (MLBPA) is going to be front and center in the news all offseason given the December 1st expiration date of the current Collective Bargaining Agreement between it and Major League Baseball itself. The MLBPA, repping the players themselves, is a labor union that wields a lot of power in brokering the future of the game on behalf of those that get on the field and play it, but there’s a whole lot more to it than just signing documents. It’s a participatory organization. The players from all 30 franchises – both major and minor league – are a very, very active part of said group. Part of that includes putting their voices together to determine their Players Choice Awards at the end of every regular season, something they’ve done every year since 1992. They announced their award winners on Wednesday morning, and Cincinnati Reds rookie Sal Stewart was tabbed the ‘Outstanding Rookie’ for the National League on the back of his 32 homer, 111 RBI breakout campaign in 2026. Since 1992, the Players Choice Awards have celebrated excellence across Major League Baseball, recognizing performance, leadership, perseverance, and impact on and off the field. The awards are especially meaningful to players, because they’re determined through a vote of their… pic.twitter.com/J3PjBkP9AP — MLBPA (@MLBPA) October 28, 2026 It’s the second significant RoY award taken home by Sal, who was also named the 2026 Sporting News National League Rookie of the Year last week. This one, though, holds a little bit more prestige and personality given that it was voted on by the players themselves. Nothing like being celebrated by a jury of one’s peers! This award, though, doesn’t come with any tangible compensation. That’s reserved for the BBWAA Jackie Robinson Rookie of the Year Award, and that will be announced on November 9th. Keep in mind that if Sal takes home that one, the Reds will be comped with an extra draft pick at the end of the 1st round in next summer’s draft (as well as the overall draft bonus pool bonus money bump that comes with it). Either way, congrats to Sal who is stacking up a pretty impressive amount of hardware after his first full season in the big leagues.

item.description: After a 4-4 start to the 2026 season, Texas A&M football has an opportunity to regroup this week before its brutal four-game gauntlet against rising SEC teams. It has been a season the Aggies wish they could forget thus far. Just one season removed from notching an 11-1 regular season record and reaching the College Football Playoff for the first time in program history, Texas A&M has its back against the ropes to try and secure bowl eligibility. Much of the downfall has come via the Aggie offense, which ranks No. 105 in the FBS in total offense, No. 72 in scoring offense and No. 129 in explosive plays of 20-plus yards. For third-year head coach Mike Elko to lead his team to the postseason and avoid having this year be a complete disaster, he must find an answer to fix the offensive woes, sooner rather than later. With just four games left to try and salvage the 2026 season, here is Texas A&M's remaining schedule and predictions for each contest on the slate: Nov. 14 - at South Carolina (4-3) Williams-Brice Stadium is one of the most intimidating and underrated college football atmospheres in the nation. Star edge rusher Dylan Stewart has played lights-out since serving a game suspension for his behavior in the Alabama game and quarterback LaNorris Sellers has been unstoppable. item.description: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has revealed Riccardo Calafiori, Noni Madueke, and Declan Rice may miss their trip to Liverpool -Credit:Darren Staples / AFP via Getty Images Arsenal's evening deteriorated further when Mikel Arteta revealed that three of his players are uncertain for Sunday's match against Liverpool. Riccardo Calafiori, Noni Madueke, and Declan Rice were absent from Tuesday's stunning Carabao Cup loss to Fleetwood Town due to injury. The Gunners were eliminated by the League Two club on penalties, despite Arteta selecting a robust starting XI because of Arsenal's mounting injury concerns. William Saliba, Bukayo Saka and Christos Tzolis are sidelined long-term, while Max Dowman will miss the weekend fixture following his reckless red card against Fleetwood. Following the match, Arteta explained why Calafiori, Madueke and Rice remained in London rather than making the journey to Lancashire for the cup encounter. "Calafiori was out, Noni was out with an ankle, and Declan was feeling a problem the other day (against Everton), which is why I had to substitute him," the Arsenal boss said, as per The Mirror . Following Saturday's 2-0 win over Everton, Arsenal sit level on points with Manchester City atop the Premier League standings and aim to extend their winning streak. But their aspirations of capturing the Carabao Cup for the first time in 34 years have already been extinguished before reaching the quarter-final round. Arteta characterized it as a 'very sad day' following the defeat to Fleetwood, whom he commended for executing what may be the most stunning upset in the tournament's history. "First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood," the Gunners boss said. "In the manner they did it, the atmosphere they created. item.title: The 1 word Connor Hellebuyck had on mind during triumphant Devils debut after Jets trade
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The 1 word Connor Hellebuyck had on mind during triumphant Devils debut after Jets trade appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Connor Hellebuyck returned to the ice for the first time since April 13, this time playing for the New Jersey Devils . Last Friday, the Devils acquired the netminder from the Winnipeg Jets after the former Hart Memorial Trophy winner requested a trade in the offseason. Hellebuyck was stellar in his debut for the Devils, as New Jersey took the 5-1 victory over the Dallas Stars. Now, Hellebuyck is explaining what was going through his head as he prepared for his first game with the Devils, per Peter Baugh of The Athletic. “Finally,” Hellebuyck thought to himself. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Hellebuyck spent 11 seasons with the Jets. In that time, he went 345-208-55 with a 2.58 goals-against average and a .916 save percentage. He requested a trade in the offseason, and then went public with the request in August. The three-time Vezina Trophy winner did not report to camp in September and was suspended by the Jets. That suspension was set to end last Friday, but the team traded him beforehand. His first appearance with the Devils brought praise from his new coach , Sheldon Keefe, according to ESPN. “He was exceptional,” Keefe said. “Not only does it seem like he’s in midseason form, but it seems like he’s been here a long time.” For his part, Hellebuyck made sure to call out the team in front of him. “The guys in front of me just played a perfect game for me to get acclimated,” he said. “Not a lot of shots, blocking everything, keeping everything to the outside. Letting me see things. Letting me touch the puck a lot.” Hellebuyck stopped 17 of 18 shots in his debut, leaving him with a .944 save percentage and his first win of the year. While most things went well, he did have one complaint. “I like the ice, but one hard part is it’s hot,” Hellebuyck said of playing in Dallas. “I sweat a lot in this game. But it’s all part of the adjustment, and it’s good to get one under me.” The Devils return to the ice Wednesday night on the road against the Colorado Avalanche. item.title: Why The Blazers’ Guards Are Working To Start The Season
item.description: Oct 21, 2026; Portland, Oregon, USA; Portland Trail Blazers guard Damian Lillard (0), left, high fives guard Ja Morant (1) during the second half in a game against the Phoenix Suns at Moda Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jimmy Vik The Portland Trail Blazers have won their first three games to start the 2026-27 NBA season. Before the season even started, the Blazers’ guards were the main topic of conversation, but with Ja Morant ‘s impact and Damian Lillard ‘s return, they are surprising the rest of the NBA. Whenever the Blazers were brought up in conversations, all the talk was just about worrying about the wonky fit of Lillard and Morant in the backcourt. It is a small sample size with three games, but they look like they have played together for multiple seasons. Blazers Head Coach Micah Nori knew the 2026-27 season would be a challenge , but he has proven to be the right hire. He has been excellent at getting the most out of the Blazers’ guards, but he would be the first person to say that the credit should be given exclusively to the players. The Blazers’ Guards Are Unselfish With Each Other Oct 23, 2026; Sacramento, California, USA; Portland Trail Blazers guard Damian Lillard (0) and Ja Morant (1) walk towards the bench in a game against the Sacramento Kings during the fourth quarter at Golden 1 Center. A lot of people pointed out that there would be a logjam with Lillard, Morant, Scoot Henderson , and Jrue Holiday . However, that has not been an issue so far this season, and it comes down to how all four players want each other to succeed. “I wish I could take credit for it, but I can’t. item.title: Why did the Kansas City Chiefs sign Justin Tucker?
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs are 5-1 to start the 2026-27 NFL season. The one area where they have struggled is the kicking game. Harrison Butker has been great for the Chiefs over the years, but he hasn’t been great for KC this season. Butker has caused drama with his comments about women and who he supports politically. Teams usually prefer their kicker to make field goals rather than cause off-field drama. He hasn’t been able to do that this year. Andy Reid isn’t afraid to sign controversial figures, and the Chiefs did just that with their most recent practice squad signing. MORE: Bold predictions for Week 8 of 2026 NFL season Chiefs sign Justin Tucker to their practice squad Jan 11, 2025; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Baltimore Ravens place kicker Justin Tucker (9) kicks an extra point against the Pittsburgh Steelers in an AFC wild card game at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Credit: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Sam McDowell of the Kansas City Star is reporting that the Chiefs have signed former Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad. He hasn’t kicked in the NFL since 2024 because he violated the NFL’s personal-conduct policy following allegations of sexual misconduct. Chiefs are signing K Justin Tucker to their practice squad, as @SamMcDowell11 reported. Tucker hasn’t kicked in the NFL since 2024 after violating the NFL’s personal-conduct policy following allegations of sexual misconduct. pic.twitter.com/fddZBV6UTE — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 28, 2026 The Baltimore Banner reported that Tucker was accused of sexual misconduct by 16 massage therapists in the Baltimore area. The NFL suspended him for 10 games in the 2025 season, and the Ravens released him in May 2025. https://t.co/E8GobOLIyf pic.twitter.com/6GiAYGVrOx — Mina Kimes (@minakimes) October 28, 2026 Tucker is one of the best kickers of all time, with a career field-goal percentage of 89.1%. Butker made 11 of 16 field goals this year and missed two big kicks in the team’s Week 7 loss to the Seattle Seahawks . The Chiefs players and staff will have to answer questions about why they’re bringing in the 36-year-old kicker. This isn’t new for Andy Reid or their star players. They’ve faced these kinds of questions before. They did the same thing when they signed punter Matt Araiza . He was named in an August 2022 civil suit that accused him of sexual assault when he was at San Diego State. The lawsuit was eventually dropped. Winning is the only thing that matters in the NFL. They’ll bring in someone with a checkered past if it gives them even a slight chance to win. Look no further than the Cleveland Browns and Deshaun Watson . According to ESPN , the new deal would see CP10 stay with the club through 2031 and would end when he is 32 years old. His current deal is set to expire at the end of the 2026-27 season and his status with the club had been undetermined until now. The news comes as Pulisic returned to his team following an injury suffered during the World Cup. As the Serie A season began, he quickly reestablished himself as a key part of the AC Milan attack and put aside doubts about him staying with the Italian giants. Pulisic’s injury recovery saw him miss the most recent USMNT international window, though his recent performances and contract extension demonstrate that he is very much a valuable asset to Mauricio Pochettino. item.description: Thierry Henry has clarified confusion surrounding his performance as Ballon d’Or presenter after attracting criticism for what he maintains were “jokes” surrounding co-presenter Kate Scott, Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal . The legendary France striker hosted ceremony for the prestigious awards in London with his CBS Sports colleague Scott, with the Champions League show’s style translating to the stage. But after correcting Scott’s pronunciation of Brazilian legend Sócrates, for which an award is named after, joking with Yamal about winning a third successive young player of the year award, despite being in contention for the main men’s award and being honest about his desire for compatriot Kylian Mbappe to beat out eventual winner Harry Kane for the main award , fans on social media criticised the former Arsenal forward’s performance. “I’ve been seeing a lot of people talking about the Ballon d’Or night and I wanted to clarify some stuff about some people getting really excited about nothing,” “First of all, Lamine Yamal, I wasn’t checking his ego at all, I just thought as the third time he’s winning that trophy, I asked him if that was the one he really wanted, and I brought out a laugh from people, we don’t know what he wanted, he didn’t get it, I’m a big fan of Lamine Yamal, I wasn’t checking his ego at all, that you didn’t like the joke, I can understand. But don’t do that, he’s one of the players I’d pay to watch, I love him, I was just asking him, if it’s the one he really wants as the real prize was coming up, unfortunately he didn’t win it, because he’s a hell of a player I’d pay to watch. “Now let’s move on to Kate, she was in on the joke, and you can ask Kate, by the way, she did it on purpose, to say Soc, and I had to say, again, you didn’t like the joke, I understand, but please stop saying I disrespected Kate, I will never do that, and you can ask her, she was on the joke with me, she did Soc on purpose, and I said Soc, so please stop inventing stories. Hosts Kate Scott and Thierry Henry on stage during the 2026 Ballon d'Or France Football award ceremony (AFP/Getty) “And the last one, if you don’t watch our show on CBS, Harry Kane, the other day, after Bayern Munich vs Arsenal, called me out for supporting Kylian Mbappe. So I just told him the other day, I’m French, and I was always going to back up and support my fellow countrymen, I said to him, you are a worth winner, you deserve it, you are the example that work ethic is a talent, working hard is a talent, I said you are a worthy winner, well done, Harry Kane, and I call him Sir Harry Kane since the World Cup. “So please, people out there, relax, relax, I love Harry Kane, I love Lamine Yamal, and I didn’t disrespect Kate, she was on the joke with me, once again, have a good night.”

item.title: 'After 2018 incident': Aaron Finch reveals how 'Sandpaper Gate' benefitted Steve Smith as a player
item.description: 'After 2018 incident': Aaron Finch reveals how 'Sandpaper Gate' benefitted Steve Smith as a player originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Former Australia captain Aaron Finch says Steve Smith became a more relaxed batter once the captaincy was taken away in 2018 after the 'Sandpaper Gate'. Finch calls Smith the best player he has shared a dressing room with. Smith missed the Cape Town Test with a neck complaint after averaging 20.75 in the series. Aaron Finch says losing the captaincy after 'Sandpaper Gate' made Steve Smith a better batter Aaron Finch has offered an unusual reading of what the 2018 ball-tampering scandal did to Steve Smith, arguing that the sanctions which cost him the Australia captaincy also removed a weight he had been carrying as a batter. Smith served a 12-month ban and a two-year prohibition on holding any leadership role, and Finch believes the second of those was the more useful. Speaking on an ESPNcricinfo show , the former Australia white-ball captain said the difference was visible as soon as Smith came back into the side. "After the 2018 incident, coming back into the international setup, Steve Smith was more relaxed as a player because he didn't have the captaincy for obvious reasons," Finch said. "As captain, so much of your time goes into things away from your own game." The particular problem, as Finch described it, was the volume of preparation Smith demands of himself and how badly that sits alongside running a team. "Getting the amount of work he wanted done put extra pressure on him mentally, because you need to get this much work done to feel ready to go, but you've still got to worry about everybody else," he added. MORE: South Africa fans wave sandpaper to mock Lyon in Cape Town Why does Finch rate Smith above every batter he has played with? Finch's wider point about Smith is less equivocal. Finch, who spent nearly a decade in Australian dressing rooms with Smith, placed him at the top of the list without much hedging. "He's the best player I've ever played with by a mile," Finch said. "He says, I'm doing it this way, I don't care what it looks like to the outside world. This is what will make me most successful." He went further on what separates Smith from contemporaries who had similar talent and similar hours in the nets. "To see what he does when others can't, you can't explain why players like me or David Warner couldn't do it, but he could. It's a natural gift, but also hard work, the hours he's put in." The Ashes of 2019 is the evidence most people reach for, and it supports Finch's case about as cleanly as any series could. Smith returned from his ban to score 774 runs in four Tests at 110.57, having missed one with concussion, and Australia retained the urn with nobody on either side within 300 runs of him. But the reality since then hasn't been that simple. MORE: What is Australia's record in Test matches without Steve Smith

item.title: Manchester United’s striker problem? Gerrard says club need a number nine who scores the ‘ugly goals’
item.description: Manchester United’s striker problem? Gerrard says club need a number nine who scores the ‘ugly goals’ Steven Gerrard has questioned whether Manchester United have a player capable of scoring 'ugly goals'. Manchester United have struggled this season and sit 16th in the Premier League table after eight games. Michael Carrick's side have taken just seven points, the club's worst-ever start to a Premier League season. United have scored just 10 goals, half the total of league leaders Manchester City. Benjamin Sesko has played just 76 minutes of Premier League football due to injury issues, with Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo deputising at centre-forward in his absence. Speaking on The Overlap Daily , Gerrard questioned whether the Red Devils have a natural goalscorer, and said United need a number nine who can score 'ugly goals'. He said past Manchester United sides have always had a forward that can bail the side out when not at their best. Steven Gerrard questions whether Manchester United have a striker who can score the ‘ugly goals’ "I just look at Manchester United's frontline, [Matheus] Cunha and [Bryan] Mbeumo. If you go back to previous Manchester United strikers, they've always had someone who is prolific. A box finisher, who can score easy goals," the former England captain said. "[Ruud] Van Nistelrooy, [Ole Gunnar] Solskjaer, [Andy] Cole, [Dwight] Yorke. Teddy Sheringham, who was more of a 10 and a nine, but scored a lot of really good goals. Then you've got [Wayne] Rooney who scored all types of goals. "I'm just not sure they've got that level of player in the frontline, who's the world-class finishes, who gets the ugly goals. So, if Manchester United don't play well, they still win, because the nine's goal an ugly goal. Like a Van Nistelrooy would get, who was a top finisher. "I do like Mbeumo a lot, and he is one of the United players who has been a positive this season."

item.title: Cris Collinsworth praises Mahomes for recovering his own fumble
item.description: The first moment arrived late in the third quarter, with Kansas City trailing Seattle 13-0. Mahomes was hit while trying to make a play, and the ball came loose as defenders closed in around him. Mahomes scrambled back toward the football and eventually recovered it after diving into the crowded pile. The effort kept the Chiefs’ possession alive, but the fumble created another setback for an offense already struggling to find momentum. Watching the sequence, Collinsworth asked, “What other quarterback is getting up twice to go get this football?” The remark sounded like praise for Mahomes’ determination, prompting criticism from viewers who believed the risk of turnovers deserved equal attention. His second comment focused on Mahomes’ expression Collinsworth’s next notable remark came after Mahomes appeared visibly frustrated following another difficult play. Instead of focusing solely on the quarterback’s execution, the broadcaster discussed the expression he had seen on Mahomes’ face. “That’s the second time I’ve seen that look on Patrick Mahomes’ face,” Collinsworth said. He connected the expression to the earlier fumble recovery, suggesting Mahomes looked as though he could not believe what was happening to him. Collinsworth then asked whether his broadcast partner had ever seen that look from Mahomes before. The observation became another talking point because the quarterback’s frustration seemed understandable given Kansas City’s offensive struggles throughout the game. Kansas City’s offensive problems made the comments stand out Mahomes finished the game with 165 passing yards, completing 19 of 33 attempts, and threw one interception. Kansas City managed only three points as Seattle’s defense controlled much of the matchup. The Chiefs struggled to sustain drives and never reached the red zone. That made the fumble sequence especially frustrating: Mahomes’ effort to recover the ball was impressive, but the original mistake had placed his team in a difficult position. For some viewers, Collinsworth’s reaction seemed to emphasize Mahomes’ resilience while giving less attention to his mistakes. Others could reasonably view the recovery as a positive individual effort during an otherwise poor offensive performance. item.title: Ravindra Jadeja loses No. 1 Test all-rounder crown after four years; Abhishek Sharma dethrones Kishan to top T20I batting rankings
item.description: Abhishek Sharma has reclaimed the No. 1 spot in the ICC T20I batting rankings, overtaking India teammate Ishan Kishan, while South Africa all-rounder Marco Jansen has become the top-ranked Test bowler and Test all-rounder for the first time in his career. Jansen's rise to the top in two categories follows his performance in South Africa's comprehensive victory over Australia in the second Test in Gqeberha. The left-arm pacer scored 85 runs with the bat and took a match-turning five-wicket haul in Australia's first innings. The performance helped Jansen improve his position across all three Test ranking categories. The 26-year-old climbed 13 places to 56th among Test batters, moved up five spots to overtake Mitchell Starc as the No. 1 Test bowler and rose one place to displace India's Ravindra Jadeja as the top-ranked Test all-rounder. Jadeja had held the No. 1 position among Test all-rounders for more than four years. Jansen's rise to the top comes after former South Africa great Dale Steyn recently described him as 'the best cricketer in the world'. Abhishek's return to the top of the T20I batting rankings came after his century against New Zealand in the third match of their series in Wellington on Tuesday. 135263294 The left-hander reached his hundred in just 35 balls and finished with 113 off 38 deliveries as India registered a six-wicket victory to seal the series. His innings helped him overtake Kishan and reclaim the No. 1 position among T20I batters. Kishan had moved to the top of the rankings in July this year after a series of good performances in Ireland. Abhishek had first reached the No. 1 spot in July 2025, when he overtook Australia's Travis Head. Several other players also moved up in the latest ICC rankings. South Africa captain Temba Bavuma climbed four places to second among Test batters after being named Player of the Match for his performance against Australia in the second Test. India captain Shubman Gill remains the top-ranked ODI batter, with Virat Kohli in third place and Rohit Sharma at No. 4.

item.title: NFL trade deadline: How the Browns, GM Andrew Berry should proceed
item.description: For the first time in a long time, the Cleveland Browns appear to be trending in the right direction . With the team sitting at 5-2, it is likely that the Browns will be buyers at the November 10th trade deadline instead of sellers. As the team prepares for their AFC North clash with the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 8, Cleveland has a rare opportunity in front of them. If the Browns were to win at Pittsburgh on Sunday, the possibility of making the playoffs would turn into a reality, considering how wide open the AFC is. GM Andrew Berry should be looking to improve their roster at the trade deadline without giving up major draft capital. Browns trade targets that don’t make sense Indianapolis Colts RB Jonathan Taylor Philadelphia Eagles RB Saquon Barkley Las Vegas Raiders EDGE Maxx Crosby Jacksonville Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr The Indianapolis Colts are having a fire sale. General manager Chris Ballard has already been fired and head coach Shane Steichen isn’t far behind. Jonathan Taylor doesn’t make much sense given the potential cost, and the Browns running game is starting to come together. The Philadelphia Eagles could be selling assets, but RB Saquon Barkley could be difficult to move because of his contract situation as well as age. It’s unlikely that the Raiders trade Maxx Crosby, but the Browns just traded away a superstar edge rusher in Myles Garrett and it wouldn’t make sense if they traded away Garrett just to trade for Crosby, who isn’t close to Garrett in terms of talent. Browns trade targets that fit for the right price Philadelphia Eagles OLB Nolan Smith Los Angeles Chargers EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu You’ll notice I’ve listed only two players here, but both are edge rushers. The Los Angeles Chargers are a disaster, and from what I was told, the team is looking to trade players to recoup draft assets. Chargers edge rusher Tuli Tuipulotu is playing on the last year of his contract and is slated to be a free agent this offseason. Acquiring Tuipulotu would boost the Browns’ edge rusher room but only for the right price. Cleveland doesn’t necessarily have to overpay to get him, but if they can, it has to be for the right price, maybe a combination of picks instead of one premium one. item.title: Justin Tucker Deserves Another NFL Chance — And the Chiefs Are Right to Give Him One
item.description: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect Justin Tucker is back in the NFL. And, yes, he deserves to be. The Kansas City Chiefs are signing the former Baltimore Ravens star to their practice squad, according to multiple reports, giving arguably the greatest kicker in NFL history his first job since Baltimore released him in May 2025. Tucker will immediately provide competition for struggling Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker. Predictably, Tucker’s return will generate controversy. It should. Sixteen massage therapists accused Tucker of inappropriate sexual behavior during massage sessions at Baltimore-area spas. Tucker denied the allegations. After conducting its own investigation, the NFL suspended him for 10 games for violating its Personal Conduct Policy. Those allegations shouldn’t be waved away because Tucker was once one of the most popular athletes in Baltimore. They shouldn’t be dismissed because he kicked a football better than almost anyone who has ever lived. But here’s the other part of the equation. Tucker served the punishment imposed by the NFL. So what exactly is supposed to happen now? The NFL Has Already Answered This Question with Deshaun Watson If the standard is that anyone disciplined for serious violations of the NFL’s Personal Conduct Policy should never play professional football again, that’s an argument someone can make. But that’s clearly not the standard the NFL operates under. Just look at Cleveland. Deshaun Watson is not merely employed by the Cleveland Browns in 2026. He’s their starting quarterback. He has started all seven games this season and is playing on the final year of the five-year, fully guaranteed $230 million contract Cleveland gave him in 2022. Watson was suspended 11 games that year after the NFL investigated allegations of sexual misconduct involving massage therapists. Watson served his suspension and was allowed to return. Tucker served his suspension and should be allowed to return, too. This isn’t an argument that one man’s alleged behavior excuses another’s. It doesn’t. It’s an argument for consistency. The NFL is filled with players who have made mistakes, exercised terrible judgment or faced serious allegations away from football. Some have been suspended. Some have been fined. Some have been released. And many have eventually received another opportunity. Tucker shouldn’t be subject to a different set of rules simply because his case became public later in his career. He was investigated. He was punished. He served the suspension. Now football should decide what happens next.
